{
  "classification": "non_routine",
  "intent": null,
  "reason": "Rejection feedback requests carry relationship and perception risk; the framing and even whether to send requires judgment about how the recruiter/company may receive it.",
  "considerations": [
    "The tone and finality of the original rejection email—was it warm, cold, or formulaic?",
    "Whether there's an existing relationship with this recruiter or if this is first meaningful contact post-rejection",
    "What specifically the candidate wants to understand (general feedback vs. feedback on particular moments in the loop?)",
    "Risk tolerance: does re-engaging risk being remembered for pushing back vs. moving on cleanly?",
    "Whether asking in general is appropriate at this company/with this recruiter (some view it as acceptable, others don't)"
  ]
}
sha256:58b8458b7d7da2213a04d64a7ed478b13:
{
  "classification": "non_routine",
  "intent": null,
  "reason": "This is an offer negotiation request to modify a core work term (remote vs. hybrid arrangement), which carries real relationship and job risk and requires human judgment on framing, timing, and tone.",
  "considerations": [
    "Whether to emphasize the family relocation as a business case or keep it private, and how much detail to share",
    "Best timing: request now (verbal offer stage) or wait for written offer and formal acceptance window",

    "Tone calibration: gratitude for the offer + confidence in the ask, without appearing ungrateful or inflexible",
    "Unknown company/manager flexibility on remote work for this level, and whether this request might jeopardize the offer"
  ]
}

  "reason": "Competing offer deadline involves strategic leverage and negotiation framing, where tone and emphasis carry real relationship risk and reflect the candidate's underlying priorities.",
